sections.title: Asking where someone was
sections.content: Hol voltál? ("Where were you?") works exactly like any other past-tense question — the question word stays in front, and volt does the rest. Negating it is just as simple: put nem in front of volt the same way you already put nem in front of van.

items.spanish: Hol voltatok tegnap? Egy koncerten voltunk.
items.english: Where were you (pl.) yesterday? We were at a concert.

sections.content: valahol ("somewhere") and sehol ("nowhere") are useful when you don't want to name the exact place: Petra sehol nem volt ("Petra was nowhere to be found"). akkor ("then, at that time") is handy for linking a past moment back to something already mentioned.
